outcome: Capability closure now preserves the exact Experiment revision snapshot it analyzed
owner_impact: Continuing capability analysis on the same Experiment revision reuses the same preserved blocked snapshot. If the Experiment has advanced to a newer revision, automatic continuation creates a new snapshot instead of silently attaching the new analysis to old artifacts. Explicitly forcing an old blocked snapshot against a newer supplied revision is rejected atomically. Continuing by blocked-snapshot ID alone keeps that snapshot's original Experiment ID, revision and artifacts. This changes snapshot integrity only; it does not approve, reject, generalize, or scientifically validate any pending capability request.

next.text: One final repair remains from the Sergio-PR-derived defect review: shared-candidate readback under permissions. It will make a reused candidate remain visible when resuming a closure even if the caller cannot read the other requester's private request row. It has not started yet.

technical_evidence: Automatic blocked-snapshot reuse now requires both the same origin Experiment and the same origin revision.
Supplying an explicit blocked snapshot together with a conflicting current origin revision raises SQLSTATE 22023 before a new closure analysis can persist.
Capability request rows now inherit origin_experiment_id and origin_experiment_revision from the immutable blocked snapshot rather than from an optional current-origin lookup.
A disposable PostgreSQL regression covers same-revision reuse, new-revision snapshot creation, stale explicit reuse rollback, and blocked-ID-only continuation preserving revision-one artifacts.
No RLS policy, candidate semantics, capability lifecycle, scientific triage state, or request decision state changes in this ticket.
